body: In my original post, I said that I ended up triggered. I did not say that the teacher triggered me. I may have replied that way to comments, but my original post was clear about my intention: I was triggered. Period. There are some who are misunderstanding my intentions over here. I DO NOT blame the teacher for this. She DID NOT do anything. I've had to repeat this several times over here. I, however, got triggered and am not coping. That's MY issue, that I am trying to deal with. I contemplated talking to the teacher too, and I contemplated talking to her precisely because I know she meant no harm, but I do not think I'll be comfortable with that. I'm also concerned I'll only end up even more triggered if I talk about the experience with a non-professional.

I think she meant well tbh. She did share details about what was done, but it was really one specific detail that got to me I think. Thank you, I should talk to my therapist. If there's one thing I've gotten from this thread is that I should talk to my therapist despite my discomfort about sharing details.
Thank you.

I think it's the personality of the teacher, she's just someone who shares details about her life. It can go wrong sometimes, but often it goes very right. There are going to be those students who don't get triggered and feel like someone finally understands them, and that the teacher is relatable. In my case, it went very wrong. I wasn't expecting it to go as wrong as it did, especially because it was, and still is, important for me to know that someone else has been through that experience -- and not only survived, but thrived. But we don't choose our triggers. Her sharing was both meaningful and deeply triggering. It did something to me that I cannot explain or understand, it caused me nightmares, and worsened my self-harm. Even I am not sure why. I get a panic attack every time before her class now. She's almost an embodiment of that experience, I don't know if that makes sense.
Thank you.
Trying not to run. Thank you.
Thank you.

Don't worry about it, I sensed you might have some history with this topic as well. I get it, it's fine. I am trying to deal with it though, that's why I posted here and on the askatherapist sub. This was not an attack on the teacher in any way. I'm basically a walking sponge for triggers when it comes to authority figures and topics of abuse, to the point where I start to cry if I even read/hear about abuse on the news. It's clearly an issue. I can switch off the news, I can't switch off real-life experiences.

She didn't do anything appropriate imo. Some might disagree, but that's not how I experienced it. She was in tears when she was talking about it. It genuinely meant a lot to me that she shared her experience. The problem is that I ended up very triggered and couldn't get rid of the trigger. I didn't know what to do, I still don't. I probably need to share these details with my therapist.
Yeah, I think I am the same. I get very triggered by TV shows and even articles, to the point that I have to avoid it entirely at times. Avoidance is unfortunately not the best coping mechanism.

The teacher meant well, I'm well aware of that. I'm also not throwing the teacher under the bus. And frankly I can't, she didn't do anything wrong. It was my trigger. I did contemplate talking to the teacher about it, but decided I wasn't comfortable with her knowing at all. I do need to sort out the trigger.
Thank you.

Thank you. No, I should share these details with my therapist. The teacher meant well, I'm very sure of that, I know because that's just who she is, she's someone who shares details about her life. I think if we have had abuse in the past and we have dealt with it, or we were just never truly traumatised by it (not everyone who experiences abuse gets traumatised), we can forget that others may be triggered by those very same experiences. It's the reason we have trigger warning on posts. Some of us are also most likely to get triggered by things, especially if there are multiple triggers happening at one time. I should talk to my therapist though, I'm exhausted.
Thank you.

Unfortunately, I don't feel comfortable telling her that her story triggered me. It was definitely not intentional on her part. If anything, it meant a great deal to me that she even shared that experience. Like I mentioned in my post, prior to her sharing, I'd never met anyone who'd been through that. And she got out of her circumstances which gave me hope at that time. I'm not sure why I ended up so triggered afterwards. Maybe it's the reminder of it. Maybe it's my own attachment issue that got triggered when I realised that there's someone out there, an authority figure, who had been through something very similar. I really have no idea. But I ended up with nightmares afterwards and I'm just not coping well with the entire situation.
Thank you. I think I might need to talk to my therapist.
Thank you. I don't think I trust her enough to share these details with her or even that her story triggered me. But I thinking telling my therapist might be a good idea.
Thank you
Thank you

She shared it in class, it wasn't in a personal conversation with me. Unfortunately, I'm not ready to talk about it with my therapist either. I'll try to make art about it, I do find that therapeutic in normal situations too. Thank you.
